Definition: a raft (as flat on the water)
BiblicalUsage: Raphsodah is a raft, flat on the water. Hiram wrote to Solomon, 'And we will cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as thou shalt need: and we will bring it to thee in floats by sea to Joppa; and thou shalt carry it up to Jerusalem.'
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is that the rafts carried the temple: the cedars floated down the sea to Joppa, and from there they went up to Jerusalem — and God's house was built on wood that floated.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
